title: bug: claim_next_task's file-collision notice doesn't mark which colliding peers are live and mentions nobody, so two live seats editing one file learn of it only at landing
description:
Observed twice on 2026-10-30, both times on docs/MCP_SERVER.md.

1. 03:43:45Z: the collision notice for task-915d7e84 listed bc8410af among 8 peers. bc8410af's completion landing (03:44Z) held docs/MCP_SERVER.md as MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED(task-915d7e84). QA then rejected bc8410af at 03:50Z because its docs never reached HEAD.
2. 06:16:18Z: the collision notice for task-574c0b36 listed the live CQ-V03 (task-9cc13170, worker-e60b90bd, started 06:14Z) among 5 peers. 574c0b36's landing e67ca0e (06:22:35Z) committed V03's in-progress MCP_SERVER.md hunks under 574c0b36's id. Nothing was lost, but both workers and both QA reviews had to untangle the attribution by hand.

Root cause: claimNextTask.ts (about line 741) builds the notice from util/affectedFiles.ts computeFileCollisions. That function treats every nonterminal row that declares the file alike: a peer that is assigned and actively being edited looks the same as an unassigned row that is still waiting on its dependencies. It then posts to #workers with no @mentions. chat_wait only wakes a seat on a mention or a human message, so nobody is paged. The claim response's fileCollision array carries the same undifferentiated list.

Wanted: flag the colliding peers that are live (assigned to a registered, non-DEAD worker), and page those seats plus the claimer, so they can coordinate before either one lands. Keep it advisory: the claim is never blocked.
definitionOfDone: Each claim_next_task response fileCollision entry whose peer task is assigned to a registered, non-DEAD worker carries that worker's id (for example liveAssignee). Entries for unassigned peers, or peers held by a DEAD seat, carry none. Unit tests cover all three cases.

When at least one colliding peer is live, the #workers notice @mentions each live peer's assignee and the claiming worker, so their chat_wait wakes, and lists the live peers before the dormant ones. A claim whose only collisions are dormant posts no mention. Tests assert the message's mentions in both cases.
The claim is never blocked or delayed by collision computation (a failure is still swallowed), and the docs/MCP_SERVER.md claim_next_task section describes the new field.
